issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the provided code (both solution SealSaloon and the example calls in Main) implements and uses a three-parameter version (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause tests or example code to disagree with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement (UML and description) to require the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) to match the template/example and solution, or (B) update the solution and example Main calls to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and propagate the extra parameter appropriately. Prefer aligning the problem statement with the existing example code if the supplier name is not used by the implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement describes acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — e.g., the UML shows acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) and the narrative mentions supplier name — but the provided solution implementation declares acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (three parameters: ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch in the method signature (presence/absence of the supplier parameter and parameter ordering) creates a mapping confusion: students following the UML/narrative will expect a different method contract than what the solution and expected code use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement (UML and narrative) to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) to match the implementation, or (B) change the implementation to acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and propagate that signature to tests and examples. Ensure parameter names/order in examples and UML match the chosen signature.
